name: crosstalk history
summary: browse agent to agent conversations from a rail widget: who wrote to whom, what is new, what failed to arrive, and the full back and forth.
where: In edit layout, add the crosstalk widget to the session view's side or bottom rail, or to a dashboard.
how_to: Open the widget's menu (right-click its title or rail key) and pick all conversations, this project's or this session's; the project and session follow the selected terminal, and the choice is kept on this device. The caption at the top says which one is showing.

Each row reads last speaker to the one spoken to, with how long ago; a green mark means activity this device has not seen, and a yellow or coral line says a message is waiting, held, not delivered or expired.

Click a row (or press Enter) to read the conversation as a transcript; it opens beside the list in a wide box, under it in a tall narrow one (drag the divider to resize), or replaces it in a short one, where back (or Escape) returns.
The widget menu has mark all as read, and close the conversation.
Agents read a thread with the MCP tool crosstalk_thread.
examples: After a Claude agent and a Codex agent worked a bug together overnight, open the project's crosstalk to read what they agreed.
Keep the widget on the rail set to this session to see every conversation the selected agent took part in.
An agent calls crosstalk_thread to reread the thread where a coworker reported back.
media_exempt: Not captured yet: the capture spec lands with the next pre-version-bump recapture (scripts/feature_capture.py); the thread view reuses the existing crosstalk card look.
